en:
Hello.
I'm Tomoharu Hosoda, Class 2-C.
Since you've all gathered here, you must know some really scary stories, huh?
{a}, was it?
Do you like scary stories too?
To tell the truth, I don't like them much.
So I don't know many scary stories, either.{p}

Honestly, I didn't really want to come.
But Hino kept insisting I join.
Hino had a reason for inviting me, you see.
I don't know many scary stories, and if anything, I'm not much good with that kind of thing.
But I've had lots of scary experiences.
I guess you could say I'm just the type who sees spirits.
Or maybe I have something about me that spirits take a liking to.
Anyway, I see them, way more than I'd ever want to.{p}

Have you ever heard that spirits are everywhere?
It's true, actually.
They really are in every kind of place.
They just drift around here and there, floating along.
There are lots of them around you, too.
You just can't see them.
You sometimes get a chill for no reason, right?
That's what you feel when a spirit happens to pass right through your body and falls into sync with you.
Most of the time they're harmless, though.
So even if the place is swarming with spirits, there's nothing in particular to worry about.
It might sound strange, but that's just how it is for people who can see them.
That said, I can't see every kind of spirit.
I can't see every last wandering spirit floating around, obviously.
If I could see that much, I'd go out of my mind.
Spirits give off an aura, you see.
I can only see the ones giving off a strong aura.
That's about the extent of my ability.
Also, even the ones without a strong aura are easier to see when there's some kind of trigger.
For example... let's see.{p}

Don't you ever see a human face in wood grain, or in a stain on a wall?
Say you visit an old house and look up at the ceiling.
You're just looking without any real thought, yet for some reason something bothers you.
One particular spot bothers you.
The grain there looks like a human face, and you can't shake it.
The face of someone writhing in agony, at that.
Have you ever had that experience?
If you have, I think you've got a strong sixth sense.
And of course, there's a spirit in that wood grain.
Then again, however much a grain or a stain looks like a face, it's often just coincidence.
What matters is when that grain or stain bothers you so much you can't stand it.
That's clear proof a spirit is calling out to you.
Of course, none of this is proven by science, and there are all sorts of opinions.
In the end, nobody can say for sure which ones are right and which are wrong.
If you see it yourself, then no matter what anyone says, it's real.
At least, that's what I think.{p}

So, spirits lurking in the grain of a ceiling or a stain on a wall.
Have I got you interested?
Naturally, this school has things like that too.
Not stains that just happen to look like faces, but stains that look like faces because a spirit really is there.
Didn't you notice?
And you seem like you'd have such a strong sixth sense, too.
You should keep your senses sharper day to day.
Do that, and I think you'd be able to pick up on it.
About those stains here at our school - there are quite a few of them.
In lots of places.
There are especially many in the old school building.
Wood grain left in strange shapes on the floorboards.
Stains soaked into the walls in sharp outline, as if something had been pressed against them.
Quite a few spirits are mixed in among them.
I don't sense anything very evil in them, though.
But the one I sense most clearly and strongly is actually in the new school building.
Do you know it?{p}

Anyone who saw it would know it's a human face.
How do I know about the girls' restroom, you ask?
I'm not a pervert or anything.
I don't go sneaking into girls' restrooms on my own.{p}

Some girls in my class came to me for advice, since they knew I had a sixth sense.
They said whenever they went into the stall closest to the window in that restroom, they got a chill.
Next to the door of that stall, there's that blackish stain shaped like a human face.
They asked me to look into it, since there might be some evil spirit there.
Of course, if you asked a teacher about something like that, they'd never take you seriously, and if you said you wanted to investigate the restroom, there's no way they'd allow it.{p}

So in the end, I snuck in.
Not by myself, though.
Of course, a whole bunch of girls came along with me, and we waited for a moment after school when nobody was around and slipped in, quick.
You might think it's a strange story, but for them it was that serious, that desperate a problem.{p}

But strangely enough, I couldn't feel a thing.
Even standing in front of the girls' restroom, I didn't sense the slightest presence.
That's why I'd never noticed it until then.
So I figured the stain in this restroom wasn't a spirit at all.
Let alone an evil one.
I thought the chill was just from a draft or something.
When I said so, the girls all seemed a little relieved.
So I thought there was no need for me to check the girls' restroom.{p}

But there was always the chance I was wrong.
Some of the girls were still looking down, anxious.{p}What would you have done?
Check the girls' restroom
Don't check it

Honestly, my heart was pounding.
About seeing the stain, of course.
Not about going into the girls' restroom.
Just so we're clear.{p}

When I went in, I thought my heart would stop.
The aura was tremendous.
It was completely different in quality from any other aura.
It didn't radiate outward; it was a dank, insidious aura that pooled up right there in that spot.
Even I could tell right away that some grudge was lingering there.
If it wasn't exorcised, something terrible was going to happen.
Even so, if I told a teacher, they'd never take it seriously.
Not until something happened...
"Hey, there IS something here, isn't there?"{p}
One of the girls caught the worry on my face and asked in a trembling voice.{p}Honestly, I wasn't sure how I should answer.
Say there's nothing there
Warn them it's better not to use this restroom
Say we should report it to a teacher

"We'd better tell a teacher.
I don't know if they'll take us seriously, but I think it's dangerous to leave it like this."
Telling a teacher probably wouldn't solve anything.
Still, it was better than not telling anyone.
That's what I thought.
When they heard what I said, the girls whispered something among themselves.
They probably knew it was a wasted effort, too.
We went to the faculty room.{p}

We went, all right, but I didn't know who to talk to.
At the time, there were four teachers still in the faculty room.{p}Who should we tell?
Ms. Hida, the student conduct teacher
Mr. Ashimura, the career guidance teacher
Mr. Wakatsuki, the P.E. teacher
Yoneyama, the math teacher

After some hesitation, we decided to talk to Ms. Hida, the student conduct teacher.
Ms. Hida is a female teacher who's strict, but really listens to what us students have to say.
You probably don't know her, though.
I told her honestly that I sensed an evil aura from the stain in the restroom, and that something should be done about it soon.
"What nonsense are you talking about?
Stop saying such stupid things and hurry home."
That was her answer.
It was exactly the answer I'd expected.
Well, at least she didn't laugh at us.
"...Sorry."
That was all we could say.{p}

It was a mistake to count on a teacher in the first place.
We'd have to do something about it ourselves.{p}

"Wait a moment."
For some reason, Ms. Hida called out to us as we were leaving the faculty room.
She had a troubled, brooding sort of look on her face.
If anything, we were the ones who were puzzled.
"Do you have a minute?
Could you wait in here?"
With that, Ms. Hida showed us to the guidance office.{p}

It was my first time there.
I'm a well-behaved student, so I'd never had any business in a place like that.
It's true, don't laugh.
We got a little worried about what was going on.
I didn't want to think they'd call our parents in or give us a harsh scolding over something like this.
Still, everyone sensed something serious in that grave look on Ms. Hida's face.
Surrounded by several girls, I waited to see what would happen.
They all looked like they were about to burst into tears.
They must have been scared of Ms. Hida.
At a time like this, I had to cheer them up, since I was the guy.
That's a man's job, right?
Just as I was thinking of telling some fun story...{p}

When she set it on the desk, it made a heavy thunk, so whatever was wrapped in that towel must have been pretty heavy.
Even after she sat down, Ms. Hida kept her hand on the towel and wouldn't let go of it.
Whatever was wrapped in it had to be very precious to her.
She looked around at all our faces, and then, as though it were hard to talk about, she told us a story.
Apparently it happened about twenty years ago.{p}

Even back then, she said, that stain was in the restroom.
There was bullying at school in those days too.
A student named Yoko Saijo was the leader of a gang of bullies.
They were always dragging timid-looking kids into the restroom and laying into them - for being cheeky, for not talking properly, for all sorts of things.
They'd twist things around - saying the kid's attitude still hadn't improved no matter how many times they'd been warned - and bully them.
Bullies don't care what the reason is.
They just pick on people they don't like, to blow off steam.{p}
And one day, Saijo took a girl over to the restroom wall, to the spot with that stain, and pressed her face against it.{p}And then she said:
Lick this stain.
You're not going home until this stain is clean.

What a horrible thing to do.
Saijo made the girl lick that stain on the wall.
Of course, the girl didn't want to.
But if she didn't do as she was told, she'd pay for it later.{p}

She cried as she did what she was told.
"Gross!
This one's actually licking a toilet wall!
Hey, doesn't this stain kind of look like your face?
Ahahahaha!"
After making her do something like that, Saijo laughed and mocked her.
Starting the very next day...{p}

Saijo stopped coming to school.
Then a week went by, then a month, and Saijo dropped out of school.
Apparently she'd come down with a serious illness and was in the hospital.
From around then, the gang of bullies Saijo had led got a lot quieter.{p}

Her family moved far away, too, apparently.
Everyone whispered that it was the curse of the restroom stain.
It might have been bad luck for Saijo, but she had it coming.
And for a while after that, the bullying stopped, too.
That's what Ms. Hida told us.
The whole time she was talking, she kept her eyes lowered.
And when she finished, she let out a long sigh and added something.{p}

"...So the stain in that restroom isn't an evil spirit.
It's a good spirit that helps children who are being bullied.
If anyone tries to do something to that stain, they'll surely be cursed.
As long as none of you do anything, it won't do any harm.
So will you leave it alone, just as it is?"
Ms. Hida asked all of us for an answer.{p}What should I say?
Leave it alone
Say it should be exorcised

"...I understand.
If that's how it is, then I have nothing more to say.
Sorry for the trouble."
Everyone nodded along with what I said.{p}

Ms. Hida had been bullied herself, back when she was in high school.
Even so, she worked hard and became a teacher.
And now she had volunteered to be the student conduct teacher, to try to stamp out bullying.
After Ms. Hida confessed something like that, there was no way we could bring up the stain again.
"You're all good kids.
I'm sorry for keeping you.
It's late, so be careful on your way home."
With that, Ms. Hida held the towel close, as if it were precious, and left the guidance office.{p}

That's when I saw it.
The towel slipped open, and inside it was a blade with a dull, leaden gleam.
It was only for an instant, so maybe I saw wrong.
But if that was a kitchen knife, what was Ms. Hida planning to do with it?
Surely, if we'd kept insisting about the stain, she wasn't going to use what was in that towel...?
...To kill us.{p}

Nah, just kidding. As if that could ever happen.
Not Ms. Hida, of all people.{p}

...But you know, even now, I find myself thinking.
Maybe Ms. Hida was lying to us.
The story about her being bullied.
And the story about a bully named Saijo being cursed by that stain and dropping out.
Wasn't the whole thing made up from the start?
Nothing like that happened twenty years ago.
I can't really explain it, but lately I can't help thinking that.
Why would Ms. Hida lie, you ask?
Well, I don't know that either.
It's just a feeling...
Maybe Ms. Hida had some reason she had to protect that stain?
Maybe she told us that lie to protect it?
I just can't shake that feeling.
I'm a guy, so I haven't been in that restroom since.
But I definitely felt an evil aura.
An incredibly evil aura.
That's no lie.
I swear to God it's no lie.
I just can't accept Ms. Hida calling that stain a good spirit.
I bet that stain has some kind of secret.
And so does Ms. Hida.
You'll probably get a chance to talk with Ms. Hida someday, won't you?
When you do... you might want to be careful.
I have a feeling something's going on there.
Well, that's just my guess, of course.{p}That's the end of my story.
Who's telling the third story?{p}

Right, that's what I figured too.
Like I said, I hadn't felt any aura at all.
And being a guy, I was a little reluctant to go into the girls' restroom.
So I didn't go in.
The girls came around to it, more or less.
But there was one who just wouldn't listen.{p}

"How can you know without even going in?
Do you really have a sixth sense or not★"
Even I got a little annoyed at that.
But what could I do?
I really didn't feel anything.
When I said so, she stuck her chest out haughtily.
"Well, I can feel it just fine."
She was so full of herself that I let slip something I shouldn't have.
"Then why don't you check it yourself!"
"Fine, I will."
......One harsh word leading to another, I guess?
She announced she'd go in by herself.
And then, of course, I got worried.
She told us to go home, but the other girls and I decided to wait outside the restroom.{p}

"What are you doing?"
Before we knew it, Tomita was standing just inside the entrance.
She was smiling, looking very pleased with herself.
"It was a spirit's doing after all.
But don't worry.
I exorcised it."
The girls rushed over to the stall by the window.
I peeked in from behind them.{p}

The wall was spotless.
So clean that I, never having seen the stain, could hardly believe there'd been one there.
All the girls kept saying,
"I can't believe it,"
over and over.
But can an amateur who just happens to have a sixth sense really perform an exorcism?
Just as I was puzzling over that...{p}

"GYAAAAAAAARGH☆"
Suddenly, letting out a scream like a beast, Tomita leapt at one of the girls.
She was on top of her, strangling her.
In a panic, I grabbed Tomita by the shoulder.
...I thought my heart would stop.
A tremendous aura came flooding into me from Tomita's shoulder.
It wasn't like a normal aura; it was dank and insidious, as though I could feel a grudge in it.
I fell flat on my backside before I knew it.
Beside me, a girl screamed.{p}

"T...Tomita's hands☆"
At the same moment, I noticed it too.
On her hands, as they strangled her friend, was a stain like a human face, clear as day.
Tomita was possessed!
When I realized that, I pulled a mop out of the cleaning closet.
I meant to hit her and knock her out.{p}

The moment I swung it back, Tomita turned around, her face twisted into something else.
This time, Tomita lunged at me.
I thought I was done for.
But the very next instant, one of the girls whacked Tomita with a mop.{p}

We got asked all kinds of questions too.
We told them as honestly as we could, but it seems they didn't believe us.
From that day on, Tomita stopped coming to school.
There were all sorts of rumors - that she'd gone into some hospital, that she'd transferred to a boarding school.
The truth?
How would I know?
But if that stain is still on her hands......
It might keep controlling her, trying to make her do something terrible.
......But I don't think that's it.
Because this year, some girls came to me again.
To tell me 'the stain is back'... in the same spot in that restroom.
That's right, the stain is still there.
I'm sure it's waiting for another victim like Tomita......{p}That's the end of my story.
Who's telling the third story?{p}

"Then why are you making that face?"
Just as I'd feared, I'd made the girls suspicious.
"Tell us the truth, come on!"
The girls crowded in on me.{p}So I......
Keep insisting it's nothing
Suggest we report it to a teacher

"Really, I'm telling you, it's nothing.
If you keep worrying about it, everything starts to look suspicious."
At times like that, don't you think it's kinder to keep on lying?
So that's what I stuck to.
In the end, the girls were convinced too.{p}

And that's how I managed to avoid getting dragged into it.
Hosoda's story was over.
I asked him a question.
"So the stain on the wall is just left there?"{p}

"Of course it is.
I mean, what could I have done about it?"
Hosoda seemed offended.
But I couldn't worry about that now.
"But that means something could happen at any time!"
No matter how you looked at it, that was far too irresponsible.
I lashed out at Hosoda.
"If anything happens, it'll be your fault, Hosoda!"
The moment I said it, I thought I might have gone a little too far.
Being told something like that might make even the gentlest person angry.{p}

With a loud crash, the club room door flew open.
We whirled around, and there stood a girl we didn't know, on the verge of tears.
"Hosoda!
In that restroom... something terrible has finally happened☆"
Hosoda quickly got to his feet.{p}

Hosoda turned around and grinned.
"...Amazing, {a}.
Just like you said, it seems 'something' really has happened......"
How could he stay so calm?
"N-never mind that, shouldn't you go and help her?"
"It's fine.
See? You can't hear her voice anymore, can you?"{p}

On the other side of the door, there was dead silence.
Had that girl gone away?
Why?
No... gone where?
As if to mock my confusion, Hosoda winked.{p}

"Let's go on with the stories.
I have a feeling something even more interesting is going to happen.
Something more interesting, and impossible to undo."
No one spoke up to refuse.
Hosoda had completely overwhelmed us.
In an atmosphere clearly different from before, Hosoda went back to his seat and propped his elbows on the table.
He looked around at our stiff faces.{p}"Now then... who's next?"{p}

"It looks like there's something very dangerous in this restroom.
You'd better not use it."
A wave of panic ran through the girls.
Honestly, I thought I'd blown it.
My bad feeling came true, and the girls burst into tears.
They must have been scared.
I get that, but just try having a bunch of girls cry right in front of you.
It made me feel like I'd done something really awful.
Knowing it was cold comfort, I said,
"Well then, why don't we try telling a teacher?
I don't know if that'll solve anything, though..."
In fact, I doubted a teacher would even take us seriously.
But if anyone saw me in a scene like that, they'd make me out to be a total villain, you know.
When I'd finally gotten them to stop crying, we all went to the faculty room together.{p}

Mr. Ashimura, the career guidance teacher, is a big, old-fashioned kind of man.
...Heh, I know what you want to say.
But hear me out to the end, will you?
The strict Mr. Ashimura apparently thought our story was a prank.
"Don't talk nonsense.
Stains in a restroom are nothing unusual.
An evil aura?
Do you enjoy scaring girls that much?!"
...Come on, isn't that harsh?
It wasn't even me who brought it up in the first place.
Anyway, we got thrown out of the faculty room.
Getting yelled at seemed to make the girls turn defiant.{p}

"Oh, let's just leave it alone.
We'll be fine as long as we stay away from it.
If anything happens, it's Mr. Ashimura's fault!"
...Girls are scary at times like that, aren't they?
They all band together in an instant.
The mood was such that I couldn't possibly raise an objection.
Well, I had no intention of going near something dangerous on purpose, either.
So we all went our separate ways.{p}

That day, my club had a meeting.
It was just a short one, but by the time it ended the sun had set.
On my way home, I suddenly found myself thinking about that restroom.
I should have left it alone, but I went out of my way to pass in front of it on my way out.{p}

And then...... can you believe it?
Mr. Ashimura was there.
Right in front of that restroom, glancing around nervously.
I ducked into the shadows on reflex.
He didn't notice me, and he went inside the restroom.{p}

And this after he'd called the story about the stain ridiculous, mind you.
Isn't that strange?{p}What would you do at a time like this?
Ignore it and go home
Peek inside the restroom

You're more timid than you look, huh.
Oh, sorry if that offended you.
I'm in no position to talk.
That's exactly what I did, after all.{p}
But you know, just as I was leaving the school building...{p}

......I heard a horrible scream.
I got scared and ran all the way home.{p}

When I went to school the next day, there were police cars there.
They said Mr. Ashimura's body had been found in that girls' restroom, dead under strange circumstances.
It was as if his body had been cut up into a bunch of parts... a dismembered corpse, I guess you'd call it.
Don't ask me why.
All I know is that the scream was probably Mr. Ashimura's.
What would have happened if I'd peeked into the restroom then?
Please, I don't even want to think about it.
The girls got scared too, and it seems they mostly stopped talking about it.
Well, that's how the career guidance teacher got replaced by the one you know now.
...You look like you're not quite satisfied.
I can't help it, there's a lot I don't understand myself.
But that's the end of my story.{p}Who's next?{p}

Curiosity always wins in the end, right?
I quietly peeked into the restroom.{p}

......I could hear a low voice.
"It's your fault... it's all your fault..."
Mr. Ashimura's voice, of course.
He seemed to be talking to the stall by the window.
"I never meant to kill you.
You're the one who fell and hit your head... so leave me alone already."
I hadn't misheard.
He said it clearly.
I was so startled I stepped back and bumped into the wall.
It was only a small sound, but he didn't miss it.{p}

The look on his face the moment he turned around...
I'd always thought he was a scary teacher, but I'd never seen a face that terrifying before.{p}

"Hosoda... you heard that?"
Mr. Ashimura came toward me.
"That stain is one of your seniors.
Years ago, I plastered her into the wall back there..."
Why do you think he told me something like that?
...Yeah. No matter what he told me, once he killed me, it would never get out... that's what it meant.
His murderous intent came straight at me.
It felt far more vicious than the aura of that stain could ever be.{p}

"...She was a delinquent.
No matter how many times I warned her, she never listened.
That time too... she just wouldn't get it, and I got so angry I hit her.
She staggered... hit her head, and died."
You're thinking I should have just run, right?
But I couldn't move.
It's embarrassing to admit, but my legs had given out.{p}

He kept coming closer and closer.
"I'll bury you next to her too... maybe she'll be satisfied once she has more company."{p}

Hair grown long, so very long, that had pushed the stall door open.
And not just his arms.
It was wrapped around his legs, his torso, and his neck too.
No matter how he struggled, it wouldn't budge.
Then the black hair started pulling him in.
"S-stop... help me..."
Maybe because his throat was being squeezed, his voice was very faint.
If I didn't help him, no one would ever notice.{p}I...
Abandoned the teacher
Helped the teacher

...I figured this was my chance, and I got to my feet.
Why should I have to save someone who tried to kill me?
"Goodbye, sir.
You'd better apologize to her in the next world..."
With that, I left the restroom.{p}
Just as I was leaving the school building...{p}
......I heard a horrible scream.{p}

When I went to school the next day, there were police cars there.
They said Mr. Ashimura's body had been found in that girls' restroom, dead under strange circumstances.
It was as if his body had been cut up into a bunch of parts... a dismembered corpse, I guess you'd call it.
I'm sure that black hair tore him apart, though.
I think the girl who was murdered, our senior, got her revenge.
The girls who'd been making a fuss about the stain must have gotten creeped out, because the rumors died out too.
Well, that's how the career guidance teacher got replaced by the one you know now.{p}That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

I couldn't just stand there and watch someone get killed right in front of me, could I?
I leapt at him and grabbed him around the waist.{p}

When I turned around, a girl was standing behind me.
She leaned over me, peering down into my face.
One look at her pale face and it was obvious she was a ghost.
The girl's lips moved.
'Take... your... hands... off...'
...Take your hands off.
It was her body buried in that wall!
I let go without thinking.{p}

The girl smiled contentedly and vanished.
She didn't look like an evil spirit to me.{p}

...So I never said anything to anyone.
After all, the murdered girl was only getting back at her killer.
Yes... after that, Mr. Ashimura was never seen again.
But you know, that stain is still filled with an aura, even now.
No, it's not that girl anymore, since she got her revenge.
I think it's Mr. Ashimura.
He kept insisting so hard that it wasn't his fault, after all.
He must still be clinging to this world, don't you think?{p}...That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

After some hesitation, we decided to go to Mr. Wakatsuki for advice.
Mr. Wakatsuki was a really kind male teacher around thirty who joked around a lot, and students all over the school adored him.
If we were going to ask anyone, we figured it should be Mr. Wakatsuki, since he was the easiest to talk to.
We shook him awake from his nap and explained the situation.
He seemed interested in our story.
He said he'd better take a look at the stain first, so we went to the restroom with him.{p}

When we went in, the powerful aura from before was still hanging in the air.
Maybe he couldn't feel it, because he walked right in looking totally unbothered.
He crouched down in front of the wall with the stain, stroking it and peering at it, examining it in his own way.
"What do you think, sir?"
He'd gone quiet, so I tried asking him.{p}And then he...
Said it was just imagination
Said it was a spirit's doing
Dodged the question
He stood straight up and answered with a laugh.{p}

"Ha ha ha!
Nothing to worry about.
This is just a stain on the wall.
If it looks like a human face, that's just your imagination.
Look at any ceiling board and you'll find stains like this all over."
We were let down.
The teacher we'd been counting on wouldn't believe a word of it.
But it couldn't be helped, right?
Any normal person would think the same.
He must not have had any sixth sense.
Otherwise, it'd be strange for him to look at that stain and feel nothing.
"Now, if you have time to be distracted by silly things like this, hurry home and study.
Exams are starting soon."
He said it with a big smile.{p}

The girls glared at me.
They'd come to me because they were counting on me, and not only could I do nothing for them, I'd gone and consulted a teacher who wouldn't even take us seriously.{p}

The next day.
I didn't want to face those girls, so I dragged my feet all the way to school.{p}

The moment I got to school, one of the girls spotted me and came running over.
That gave me a jolt.
I thought she must still be furious about yesterday.
But that wasn't it.{p}

"Hosoda, Hosoda!
Something awful's happened!"
"What's wrong?
I can't understand unless you calm down and tell me."
This is what she told me.
"Mr. Wakatsuki's been acting weird since yesterday."
"Huh? Mr. Wakatsuki?★"{p}

"My whole upper body, except from the neck up and from the wrists down... That was the gift it talked about."
I felt like I finally understood why Ms. Hida only ever wore long-sleeved blouses, even in midsummer.
"I don't know what that thing is.
But even without my body, I'm still alive like this...... in this state."
The hair on the back of my neck seemed to stand on end.
If it had that kind of power, it was no ordinary evil spirit.
It had to be something far more powerful and evil, something monstrous.
Like... a demon, say.{p}

"...So please.
I want you to stay away from there.
I became a teacher so that I could keep watch over that restroom and make sure nothing like this ever happens again."
We nodded at Ms. Hida's words.
It wasn't a problem we could do anything about.
We promised not to use that restroom and to keep what we'd heard that day a secret, and then we went home.{p}

......Huh? You're asking if it's really okay for me to tell this here?
Yeah... Actually, there's something that's been bothering me.
A girl in my class has been missing since the day before yesterday.
On top of that, the girl who was her best friend has been coming to school in a long-sleeved cardigan since yesterday.
She said she'd caught a cold, though.
Yeah, it's probably just what you're thinking.
The girl in the cardigan is one of the girls who heard Ms. Hida's story with me.
I don't know whether there's a body under that cardigan of hers.
But maybe...
There's one more thing that's bothering me.
I wonder if the stains in that restroom have multiplied again......{p}That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

"...But I can't believe that thing is a good spirit.
It'd be better to exorcise it before something bad happens."{p}

In that instant, Ms. Hida's expression changed.
Her eyebrows shot up, she bit her lip, and she stared at me with bloodshot eyes.
Do you know the hannya, the Noh mask?
They say it's the face of a woman consumed by evil thoughts who has turned into a demon.
Ms. Hida's face looked just like it.
I'm not proud of it, but I'm not exactly the bravest type.
I was shaking all over.
If I hadn't been with the girls, I might have run away right then and there.{p}

But then Ms. Hida suddenly looked down.
"I see... It's a shame you don't understand."
The strange, possessed glint in her eyes had faded, too.
With her shoulders slumped, Ms. Hida looked like she'd turned back into a girl our own age.
"...If it's going to be exorcised, then at least let it be by my own hands... I want to exorcise it with all my heart, hoping it can rest in peace..."
Ms. Hida had a strong sense of justice, so I guess that's why she felt that way.
She looked at me and smiled weakly.{p}

"You seem to know a lot about spirits, Hosoda.
Will you tell me what I should do?"
Of course, I didn't know the first thing about exorcism.
But seeing how lonely she looked, I started to feel like I was doing something wrong.
"If it's something I can do..."
"Thank you."
She looked somehow relieved.
I sent the girls home first, and sat down facing her.{p}Now, what should I do?
Ask for more details about Saijo
Ask what the stain really is
"Don't you know anything at all about what happened to this Saijo?"{p}

At my question, Ms. Hida smirked.
"How should I know?
I'd be glad if she'd dropped dead in a ditch somewhere."
I was stunned.
Ms. Hida looked like a completely different person.
As if someone had flipped a switch.
When I didn't say anything, she rose unsteadily to her feet.
"The girl who was made to lick the stain... was me. Me, back when I was still a student."
As she said that, she picked up the bundle wrapped in the towel.
What came out of it was a kitchen knife that looked very sharp.
Even then, I still didn't understand what was happening.
I mean, she was a teacher.
But that same Ms. Hida pointed the knife at me.{p}

"That stain with Saijo's face was my curse.
After I licked that stain, a strange power to curse people awoke in me..."
She talked about these horrifying things in a perfectly flat voice.
She was supposed to be a teacher I knew well, but it was like meeting someone for the first time.
"Ever since, I've been cursing the people I hate.
Those I cursed fell ill or got hurt.
That's why I can't let that stain be destroyed!"{p}
But it wouldn't open.{p}

"I locked it, you little fool.
Anyone who tries to take that stain away from me, I'll kill them, whoever they are☆"
Ms. Hida's face had turned into the hannya again.
"Now, prepare yourself!"
She raised the knife high.
Ms. Hida, wearing a look that didn't seem human, came charging at me.{p}

I squeezed my eyes shut and crouched down.
Wham! A powerful impact hit my back!
That crash must have been the sound of my life ending.
I was dead.
Goodbye, Dad! Goodbye, Mom!
.........Then, with a start, I realized.
I wasn't dead at all.{p}

When I fearfully opened my eyes, in front of me was the lower half of a body in a skirt, hanging limply.
Following it upward with my eyes, I saw that the upper half had smashed through the glass of the door and was sticking out the other side.
Drip... drip... Warm blood fell onto my face.
Even when I peered at her, Ms. Hida didn't move. Her eyes had rolled back, and her face was full of resentment.
Apparently she'd cut her carotid artery on a shard of glass.{p}

Things got rough after that.
My legs gave out, so I was alone with Ms. Hida's corpse until the teacher on night duty found us.
In the end, they put it down to Ms. Hida having a nervous breakdown.
Well, she was a serious person, after all.
What happened to the stain, you ask?
Actually, it's still in the same spot.
Lately, if you go near the stain, you can hear a woman crying... There's even a new rumor like that going around.
Some people say the voice sounds like Ms. Hida's.
As for me, I've had enough of being inside girls' restrooms.{p}That's the end of my story.
Now, who's next?{p}

"Ms. Hida, do you know what that stain really is?"
At my question, Ms. Hida nodded.
"Yes... Well.
I suppose I can tell you, Hosoda."{p}
The moment she said that, she pulled out what was inside the towel and raised it high.{p}
The instant I looked up at that... dully gleaming hammer, a heavy blow came down with a crack, and I passed out.{p}

When I came to, I was tied up, wrapped round and round.
It was dark all around me.
Had the sun gone down while I was unconscious?
"I see you're awake."
It was Ms. Hida's voice.{p}

Looking around from my cramped position, I saw that I was inside that girls' restroom.
Ms. Hida was gently stroking the stain on the wall as she watched me.
"The story I told you earlier isn't true.
But it isn't a complete lie, either."
What was she talking about?
Her voice was quiet, but eerie.
"Saijo wasn't really the bully. That's the name of the girl who was made to lick the stain.
The bully's real name was Hida..."
Hida★
Shocked, I looked up at her.
"I'll tell you what really happened back then.
Watching Saijo cry was so much fun that I shoved her against the stain on the wall......
And then the stain moved.
As if it were alive. It was beautiful."
Ms. Hida wasn't looking at me at all.
She seemed entranced, lost in some lovely memory.
"In an instant, the stain spread, and a huge mouth opened in the middle.
Can you believe it, Hosoda?"
Even now, as I tell you this, I bet you can't believe it.
But I could.{p}

Because right then, the stain twitched, as if it were reacting to her voice.
"Hee hee... This little one is happy too.
It seems to have taken a liking to you, Hosoda."
The stain had taken a liking to me...
I knew what that meant, and why the stain was happy.
Lying there on the floor, I tried to crawl away.
But she caught me right away.{p}

"You mustn't run away.
You're going to go join Saijo now."
So I was right.
I felt like I was about to faint.
Ms. Hida roughly pulled me to my feet and shoved me toward the stain.{p}

"Here you go... your first meal in a long time."
At the delight in Ms. Hida's voice, something in my mind snapped.
I screamed and thrashed my body back and forth.
Like a little kid throwing a tantrum and refusing.
She'd let her guard down, and she lost her balance.
And then......{p}

Even now, I feel sick when I remember that moment.
The stain that had been about to eat me must have been waiting with its mouth wide open.
And unluckily for her, Ms. Hida fell right into it.
You can guess what happened, right?
I desperately worked the rope loose.
What if the stain peeled off the wall and came after me... I was scared of that.
I was so scared, I don't even remember how I got home.
In the end, Ms. Hida was listed as missing.
The stain ate its meal without leaving a single crumb... I guess that's what it means.
...Is the stain still there, you ask?
Who knows. I never want to go near that place again.
But if that thing is alive, and Ms. Hida was the one bringing it food...
Then it can't have eaten anything since she disappeared.
It's either dead or weak... or maybe it's moved somewhere else, looking for food.{p}That's the end of my story.
Who's going to talk next?{p}
